Muse with Violin screen, Rose Iron Works

Paul Fehér’s wrought-iron fire screen for the Rose Iron Works of Cleveland: a gilded violinist in a stepped, silvered frame of arches and stylized leaves on dark blue velvet.

Source
Cleveland Museum of Art: Muse with Violin Screen, 2020.216
Creator

Made

Style

Context

The museum gives the date 1930, the materials steel, brass, silver and gold plating, and cotton velveteen, and the size 156.2 × 156.2 cm. Cleveland Museum of Art.

The museum text says Martin Rose founded the Rose Iron Works after training in Vienna, hired the Parisian designer Paul Fehér in the 1920s, and describes the screen’s geometric patterning, stylized natural forms, and a central figure reminiscent of Josephine Baker as “the classic motifs of Art Deco design”. Cleveland Museum of Art.

The screen was shown in the museum’s May Show of 1930 and reproduced in Arts and Decoration in January 1931, according to the museum’s exhibition and citation lists. Cleveland Museum of Art.

Observed

  • The screen is nearly square, with a tall central panel between two narrower side panels, all framed in hammered silver-colored metal.
  • The central panel holds a gold nude figure playing a violin, standing on a mound of wavy lines, inside a frame of stacked semicircular arches.
  • Stepped, right-angled bars in the side panels climb in tiers and carry stylized leaf sprays.
  • A row of short vertical bars forms a stepped cresting along the top; the feet are grooved blocks.
  • The metal is set against dark blue velvet, so the silver ornament reads as bright line on a deep ground.
  • The layout is mirror-symmetrical about the central figure.

Why it belongs

This is a near-perfect rubric match for the style: symmetry, stepped outlines, arches in regular rhythm, and metal on a dark jewel tone.

It shows the Paris idiom carried to an American industrial metalworks within five years of the 1925 Exposition.

Borrow

Frame a central panel with stacked semicircles on each side, like a column of arches.

Use a deep blue ground and draw all ornament in one metallic tone, with a single gold element at the center.
